page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-2 is a dual-vCPU virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 7B13 processors using the x86_64 architecture. The instance configuration allocates 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core with multithreading enabled, supported by dedicated CPU allocation. Cache hierarchy features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, while AVX-512 and AMX instructions are absent.

Memory capacity is provisioned at 16.0 GB, yielding a high ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance comes with no bundled local storage and no integrated GPUs, requiring persistent disks or external network storage for stateful storage needs. Network connectivity lacks complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate adequate baseline execution on single-threaded tasks alongside capacity constraints in multi-core throughput. The instance recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 1490.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 2678.19, both aligning with median benchmark tiers. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 25.75 GB/sec. Due to the two-vCPU ceiling, multi-core benchmarks scale modestly, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 1838.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 3087.26. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth registered at 31.35 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 22.01 GB/sec. Database operations under PassMark scored 851.1, while Redis SET operations achieved 2.0 million operations per second.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, n2d-highmem-2 provides cost-effective access to large memory allocations without requiring over-provisioning of CPU cores. The primary operational tradeoff is constrained compute parallelism, which limits static web throughput to 2.52 GB/sec and restricts dense algorithmic processing. The server is well suited for memory-centric microservices, low-throughput in-memory caching, staging environments, lightweight database read replicas, and memory-bound background tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-2 is a general-purpose, memory-leaning virtual instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 x86_64 processor. It provisions 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single multithreaded physical core alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, delivering a generous 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration excludes local disk storage and hardware GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached volumes for data persistence. Benchmark evaluations show steady single-core responsiveness, achieving a 1490.0 Geekbench single-core score and 25.75 GB/sec gzip compression throughput. However, overall multi-core performance is constrained by the two-vCPU count, as reflected in an 1838.0 Geekbench multi-core score and modest memory bandwidth figures (31.35 GB/sec uncached read). Without bundled local disks or hardware accelerators, this server delivers qualitative resource efficiency for memory-intensive workloads with moderate compute demands, including small in-memory datastores, lightweight caching layers, backend microservices, and general staging deployments.
